files.rationale: Adds section 38: the tonal score and the shadow scale. Each banded section redefines the theme tokens on itself rather than setting colours, so the whole subtree follows. Also fixes the chat launcher and Send button, which set color:#fff over var(--primary-color) and rendered at contrast 1.49 on the dark theme's mint. Follow-up: .chat__msg--user carried the same bug and was found only by re-auditing with the panel open.

Nine legacy rules under html.light-theme hardcoded #0F172A and #475569 from the superseded blue theme. A literal cannot follow a section that overrides the tokens, so project titles rendered at contrast 1.31 on the new dark band. All nine converted to var(--text-primary) / var(--text-secondary), which INV-STYLE-002 already required. Resolved values are unchanged outside a band.
Cache-busting version only, bumped to 20260920-bands across 12 links. No markup change: the bands are applied by section id, so the tonal score needed no new classes.
Cache-busting version only, 3 links. The CV shares styles.css, so it has to pick up the token conversion.
The next free CSS section number was stale at 30 and is now 39, with a pointer to INV-STYLE-004 so the next person writing a band redefines tokens instead of colours.
INV-STYLE-004 records the band mechanism. The literal-colour trap is recorded beside the specificity one, because INV-STYLE-002 had forbidden it since bootstrap and nothing enforced it.
Records the dark-theme contrast fix on the launcher and the Send button. The bug shipped with TASK-001 and was found by the audit run here.

Out-of-scope discovery: .neural-atmosphere is a complete second background system that no page references and no script injects. Recorded rather than deleted, because removing a block of CSS does not belong in a task whose diff should read as what changed visually.
